# `silk/mem/va_list`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The C variadic arguments of an `export "C"` function, read one at a time.

## When to use
Use [`VaList`](#VaList) in the body of an `export "C"` function whose parameters end with `...`, such as
a C library entry point like `uv_loop_configure(loop, option, ...)` that a C program calls with
extra arguments.

## Details
The function's C entry starts its `va_list` before the body runs. `Intrinsic.variadicArguments()`
answers its address in that body only, and [`VaList.of`](#VaList.impl.of) wraps it. Each [`VaList.next`](#VaList.impl.next) reads
the next argument as the C caller passed it, under the target's C ABI: System V x86-64 and AAPCS
ARM64 read the register save area and then the stack, while Darwin ARM64, Windows and
WebAssembly read consecutive stack slots. A type implements [`VariadicArgument`](#VariadicArgument) to say how C
passes it; the integer types, `f64` and the raw pointers of [`VaList.nextPointer`](#VaList.impl.nextPointer) are covered.

C promotes a variadic `char` or `short` to `int` and a `float` to `double`, so read those as
`i32` and `f64`.

## Gotchas
Nothing checks the C caller: reading more arguments than it passed, or a type other than the
one it passed, reads unrelated memory. The list lives in the C entry's frame, so it is valid only
until the function returns; do not keep it or its address.

## Examples
### Read one `int` when the option asks for it
```silk
import silk.mem.va_list { VaList }

pub unsafe export "C" fn configure(target: *mut u8, option: i32, ...) -> i32 as "example_configure" {
  if option != 0 {
    return 0
  }
  unsafe {
    let mut arguments = VaList.of(Intrinsic.variadicArguments())
    return arguments.next<i32>()
  }
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return 0
}
```

Import as `VaList` with `import silk.mem.va_list { VaList }`.

## `VaList`

```silk
pub struct VaList
```

The C variadic arguments of the running `export "C"` function, read in order.

### Details

Make one with [`VaList.of`](#VaList.impl.of) from `Intrinsic.variadicArguments()` in the body of an `export "C"`
function whose parameters end with `...`. Each [`VaList.next`](#VaList.impl.next) reads one argument under the
target's C ABI and moves past it. The list lives in the function's C entry frame and is valid
until the function returns.

## `VariadicSlot`

```silk
pub struct VariadicSlot<T>
```

How C passes a variadic argument of type `T`: in an integer or a floating-point slot, and how
many bytes the value has.

### Details

[`VariadicArgument`](#VariadicArgument) answers one for each type that [`VaList.next`](#VaList.impl.next) reads.

```silk
pub floating: bool
```

Whether C passes the value in a floating-point register when one is free.


<a id="VariadicArgument"></a>

## `VariadicArgument`

```silk
pub interface VariadicArgument
```

A type that a C caller can pass as a variadic argument after C's default promotions, so that
[`VaList.next`](#VaList.impl.next) can read it.

### Details

`i32`, `u32`, `i64`, `u64`, `isize`, `usize` and `f64` implement it. A narrower C integer arrives
as `int` (`i32`), and a `float` arrives as `double` (`f64`).

<a id="VariadicArgument.variadicSlot"></a>

### Operation `variadicSlot`

```silk
fn variadicSlot() -> VariadicSlot<Self>
```

How C passes a value of this type.

<a id="VaList.impl.of"></a>

### Associated function `of`

```silk
pub unsafe fn of(list: *mut u64) -> VaList
```

Wraps the `va_list` at `list`, the address `Intrinsic.variadicArguments()` answers in the
body of an `export "C"` function whose parameters end with `...`.

#### Details

The list starts at the first variadic argument. It lives in the function's C entry frame, so
the result is valid until the function returns.

<a id="VaList.impl.next"></a>

### Method `next`

```silk
pub unsafe fn next<T: VariadicArgument + Copy>(self: &mut Self) -> T
```

Reads the next variadic argument as a `T` and moves past it.

#### Details

It follows the target's C ABI for a value that C passed as `T` after the default promotions:
a `char` or `short` arrives as `i32` and a `float` as `f64`. The caller must have passed an
argument of this type in this position; nothing checks it.

<a id="VaList.impl.nextPointer"></a>

### Method `nextPointer`

```silk
pub unsafe fn nextPointer<T>(self: &mut Self) -> ?*mut T
```

Reads the next variadic argument as a raw pointer to `T`, which may be null, and moves past
it.

#### Details

The caller must have passed a pointer in this position; nothing checks it.
